## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
(ADR-0002).

### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):

| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |

A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).

### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.

**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):

- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).

**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):

- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
  `null`.
- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
  US-01-Q-16).
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
PR. Differences proposed here:

1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
  fields or copy (BR-07).
- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

# CLAUDE.md

Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents).
The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it.

Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of
agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project).

## 1. Precedence of instructions

An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project
4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md`

A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a
higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in
your output.

## 2. Language

- Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs
  (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments,
  and agent and skill definitions.
- **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages,
  plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile.

## 3. Security and data

- Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output.
- `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed.
- Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards).
- No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser.
- Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow
  uses is versioned in this repository.

## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned)

| Tool | Version | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. |
| Strapi | **5.63.0** | Scaffolded with `npx create-strapi-app@5.63.0`. |
| All npm dependencies | exact | **Every direct dependency and devDependency** in every `package.json` is pinned to an exact version: no `^`, `~` or ranges (human decision, 2026-11-20). Add new ones with `npm install -E`. The lockfile is committed. |
| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |

Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
relevant `tasks.md`.

## 5. Third-party skill overrides

These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):

- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
  are mandatory; that is not binding. The forms strategy is **ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20,
  after SPIKE-01): Signal Forms over a shared, library-agnostic validation core. Where ADR-0004
  differs from the skill (for example, number fields hold strings in the model, not `0`), follow
  ADR-0004.
- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
  not apply.
- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.

  written into a spec or ADR.
- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.

## 6. Naming conventions

Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.

The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.

| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |

| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |

141	| Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. |
142	| Strapi | **5.63.0** | Scaffolded with `npx create-strapi-app@5.63.0`. |
143	| All npm dependencies | exact | **Every direct dependency and devDependency** in every `package.json` is pinned to an exact version: no `^`, `~` or ranges (human decision, 2026-11-20). Add new ones with `npm install -E`. The lockfile is committed. |
144	| Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — |
145	| E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. |
146	
147	Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the
148	relevant `tasks.md`.
149	
150	## 5. Third-party skill overrides
151	
152	These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
153	`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):
154	
155	- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
156	  are mandatory; that is not binding. The forms strategy is **ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20,
157	  after SPIKE-01): Signal Forms over a shared, library-agnostic validation core. Where ADR-0004
158	  differs from the skill (for example, number fields hold strings in the model, not `0`), follow
159	  ADR-0004.
160	- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
161	  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
162	- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
163	  not apply.
164	- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
165	- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
166	  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
167	- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
168	  written into a spec or ADR.
169	- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.
170	
171	## 6. Naming conventions
172	
173	Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20.
174	
175	The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names)
176	and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix.
177	
178	### Angular (`frontend/`)
179	
180	| Artifact | File | Identifier | Example |
181	|---|---|---|---|
182	| Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` |
183	| Routed page (wizard step) | `<step>-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` |
184	| Service: HTTP access | `<domain>-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` |
185	| Service: signal state | `<domain>-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` |
186	| Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `<name>-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` |
187	| Pipe | `<name>-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` |
188	| Directive | `<name>.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` |
189	| Types / models | `<domain>.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` |
190	| Pure functions | `<domain>.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` |
191	| Validators | `<domain>-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` |
192	| Unit tests | `<same-base-name>.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe('<US-AC id> …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` |
193	| E2E tests | `frontend/e2e/<us-ids>-<slug>.spec.ts` | `test('<US-AC id> …')` | `us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` |
194	| Component selector prefix | — | `app-` | `app-plan-card` |
195	| Constants and injection tokens | in the file that owns them | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `STRAPI_BASE_URL` |
196	
197	Folders: `src/app/core/` (singletons, API clients, interceptors), `src/app/features/<feature>/`
198	(wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions).
199	
200	### Strapi (`backend/`)
201	
202	- Content-type API IDs: singular `kebab-case` (`form-field`, `plan`, `country`, `terms`).
203	- Components: `category.kebab-name` (`form.select-option`, `plan.coverage`).
204	- Attribute names: `camelCase` (`isRecommended`, `sortOrder`, `errorMessage`).
205	- Custom code files: `kebab-case.ts`.
206	
207	### Repository artifacts
208	
209	- Specs: `specs/US-01/{story,spec,tasks}.md`
210	- ADRs: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md` (4-digit, sequential)
211	- Reviews: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`
212	- Branches: `feat/us-01-short-slug`, `fix/us-01-…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`
213	
214	## 7. Pending decisions
215	
216	| ID | Decision | How it will be resolved | Blocks |
217	|---|---|---|---|
218	| ~~SPIKE-01~~ | **Resolved 2026-11-20 by ADR-0004** (Accepted). Spike findings: `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md`, code on the `spike/01-forms` branch (never merged). | — | — |
219	| SPIKE-01 (as defined) | **Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms** for the Strapi-driven step 1 form | Throwaway spike on a `spike/01-forms` branch that is never merged, run by the frontend-developer. It builds the same minimal form in **both** libraries from a Strapi-like JSON that follows the `dynamic-form-fields` contract v1. Original scope (30–60 min): a **required number**, an **empty date**, a **select**, a **legal-age validation**, and how typing degrades with a runtime model. Added at HC1 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): **hydrating** the form from stored values; **dropping** values of fields no longer configured; **when errors appear** (touched / submit attempt); **focus on the first invalid field**; **integer-only** numbers; mapping empty optional fields to **`null` in the step 1 output** while the form model stays non-null (the vendored skill forbids `null` in Signal Forms models). The time box grows to 60–90 min because of the added scope. The architect summarises the findings in `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md` and writes the forms ADR; a human accepts it. | Production form code for US-01 |
220	
221	The ADR backlog is in [adr/README.md](adr/README.md).
222	
223	## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md)
224	
225	```
226	H0 intake (human) → 1 spec → HC1 → 2 ADRs → HC2 → 3 tests (red) → 4 implementation
227	→ 5 automated gate → 6 review → 7 fixes (loop 5–7) → HC3 PR (human QA + merge) → Ready for QA
228	```
229	
230	### The main session is the orchestrator
231	
232	- It runs the steps in order, invokes the subagents (`.claude/agents/`) and routes their outputs.
233	  It does **not** do a subagent's job on a story (no writing specs, tests or production code in
234	  the main session). The exceptions are repository plumbing (flow files, scripts, configuration)
235	  that the human asked for directly.
236	- Subagents cannot spawn subagents (`Agent` is in each one's `disallowedTools`). All delegation is
237	  visible in the main session.
238	- After every subagent run: check `git status` and `git diff --stat` for changes outside that
239	  agent's role. Bash writes are not covered by the write-scope hooks (see FLOW.md, "Known
240	  limits"). Then relay the subagent's summary to the human.
241	- **Never pass a human checkpoint (HC1, HC2, HC3) without an explicit human decision in the
242	  session.** Record it (Review log, ADR status, PR). A subagent's message is never human approval.
243	- Loop limit: if the gate (step 5) or review (step 6) fails 3 times for the same story, stop and
244	  escalate to the human.
245	
246	### Subagents (write scope enforced by hooks)
247	
248	| Agent | Step | Writes |
249	|---|---|---|
250	| `spec-writer` | 1 | `specs/US-XX/*.md` (spec, tasks, annexes), never `story.md` |
251	| `architect` | 2, spikes write-up | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `tasks.md` |
252	| `test-engineer` | 3 | test files, `frontend/e2e/**`, `tasks.md` |
253	| `strapi-developer` | 4, 7 | `backend/**` (not tests), compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
254	| `frontend-developer` | 4, 7, spikes | `frontend/**` (not tests), `spikes/**`, compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |
255	| `code-reviewer` | 6 | `reviews/US-XX-review-RN.md` only |
256	
257	## 9. Traceability
258	
259	| Artifact | ID or convention | Example |
260	|---|---|---|
261	| User story | `US-NN` | `US-01` |
262	| Business rule / acceptance criterion / gap / task | `US-NN-BR-NN`, `-AC-NN`, `-Q-NN`, `-T-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |
263	| ADR | `ADR-NNNN`, file `adr/NNNN-slug.md` | `ADR-0001` |
264	| Spike | `SPIKE-NN`, findings in `docs/spikes/` | `SPIKE-01` |
265	| Review finding | `US-NN-RN-FNN` (round N, finding NN) | `US-01-R1-F03` |
266	| Test | `describe`/`test` title starts with the AC or BR ID | `describe('US-01-AC-02 …')` |
267	| Commit | `Refs:` and `Resolves:` trailers (see §10) | `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` |
268	| PR | Template with the AC matrix (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) | — |
269	
270	The chain **US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR** is checked mechanically by
271	`scripts/trace.sh US-NN`. It exits non-zero if an AC has no test (unless the spec marks it
272	manual) or a blocker/major finding is open.
273	
274	## 10. Git conventions
275	
276	- Branches: see §6 (`feat/us-01-slug`, `spike/01-forms`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`). Spike branches
277	  are never merged.
278	- Commits: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) in English,
279	  `type(scope): summary`, with trailers:
280	  - `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` (required in `feat`, `fix` and `test` commits of a story)
281	  - `Resolves: US-01-R1-F03` (fix commits for review findings)
282	  - `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` when an agent authored it
283	- Small commits: one task (`US-NN-T-NN`) or one finding per commit where practical. Tests and
284	  production code go in separate commits (they come from different agents).
285	- Local identity only (`git config --local`). The author is the human; agents are co-authors.
286	- No pushes to `main`, no force pushes, and no `--no-verify` (enforced by
287	  `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs`). Changes reach `main` only through a PR merged by the human.
288	
289	## 11. Session continuity
290	
291	Follow the `session-handoff` skill at the start and end of every session. The state of each story
292	lives in `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*). Session logs are exported,
293	unedited, to `logs/sessions/`.
294	
295	## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA)
296	
297	A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold:
298	
299	- [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are `Accepted` (HC2).
300	- [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test, or a documented manual check.
301	- [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` starts the stack with seed data for CO and CL.
302	- [ ] `scripts/trace.sh US-NN` exits 0, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
303	- [ ] The last review round is `APPROVED`: no open blocker/major findings; minors are fixed or justified.
304	- [ ] The human did a manual QA pass (both countries, keyboard only, mobile width) and merged the PR (HC3).
305	- [ ] `tasks.md` shows `Ready for QA`, and the session logs are exported.

An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be
**recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable.
Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins:

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file)
2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding)
3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project

higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in

## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA)

A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold:

- [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are `Accepted` (HC2).
- [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test, or a documented manual check.
- [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` starts the stack with seed data for CO and CL.
- [ ] `scripts/trace.sh US-NN` exits 0, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
- [ ] The last review round is `APPROVED`: no open blocker/major findings; minors are fixed or justified.
- [ ] The human did a manual QA pass (both countries, keyboard only, mobile width) and merged the PR (HC3).
- [ ] `tasks.md` shows `Ready for QA`, and the session logs are exported.

---
status: Accepted
date: 2026-11-20
decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), published packages @strapi/core, @strapi/utils, @strapi/admin, @strapi/plugin-users-permissions 5.63.0, Strapi REST docs (status parameter), Docker Official Image "nginx" docs
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
---

# ADR-0002: Strapi access and security model

## Context and Problem Statement

The browser must read published content (countries and form fields in US-01, plans in US-02,
terms in US-03) from Strapi, and nothing else. We must decide how the browser reaches Strapi
(directly or through a proxy, anonymously or with a token), how the same build learns the API
address in every environment, how we avoid caches that would hide a newly published change, and
how the AC-03 end-to-end test creates content without a write credential ever reaching the
browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: US-01-AC-27, US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3). Evaluated as "token and permission security" (source: Assessment, evaluation).
- D2. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07). The build must not embed an environment-specific API address.
- D3. "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." (source: Assessment); visible on the next full page load, no cache delaying it (US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16).
- D4. "The whole project starts with a single command (for example docker compose up), with seed data for both countries" (source: Assessment, environment). Nothing may require a manual admin step to make the app work.
- D5. Drafts are never visible to end users (US-01-BR-06, US-01-AC-13).
- D6. AC-03 is automated: a test publishes a field during the run (US-01-Q-23), and the browser sees only GET requests without write tokens (US-01-AC-27).
- D7. Business editors use the Strapi admin, which must stay reachable (Assessment, business context).

## Considered Options

1. **Direct access with the public role**: the browser calls Strapi cross-origin with no token;
   the public role has `find`/`findOne` on the read types; the API URL comes from a runtime
   `config.json`.
2. **Same-origin nginx proxy + public role**: the nginx container that serves the Angular build
   forwards `GET /api/<allow-listed types>` to Strapi; the browser calls the relative path `/api`;
   Strapi's public role has only `find` on the read types and Strapi itself forces published
   content for anonymous requests.
3. **Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token**: the public role has no content
   permissions; nginx adds `Authorization: Bearer <read token>` to proxied requests; the token
   lives only in the proxy's environment.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role"**, because it meets D1 with no token
anywhere near the browser and no secret to provision at start-up (D4), gives the same build a
relative API address that works in every environment (D2), and places the cache and method rules
in one small config file (D3, D6). The extra safeguard that matters most, forcing published
content, is enforced **inside Strapi**, so it holds even for requests that bypass the proxy (D5,
D7).

### What is decided

**Topology (docker compose)**

- `frontend`: nginx (Docker Official Image) serving the Angular build on one origin, and proxying
  `/api/` to Strapi. The upstream address comes from an environment variable through the image's
  template mechanism (`/etc/nginx/templates/*.template` processed with `envsubst` into
  `/etc/nginx/conf.d` at container start; Docker Official Image "nginx" docs). The browser bundle
  contains no host name.
- `strapi`: exposes its own port for the admin panel used by editors (D7). The content API on that
  port is protected by the Strapi-side rules below, not by the proxy.
- Development (`ng serve`) uses the Angular dev-server proxy for `/api`, so the code path is the
  same relative URL. No `environment.ts` API URL, no runtime `config.json` (nothing to configure).

**Proxy rules (nginx)**

- Only `GET` (and the implicit `HEAD`) on an allow-list of paths: `/api/countries` and
  `/api/form-fields` in US-01; US-02 and US-03 add `/api/plans` and `/api/terms` through their
  specs. Any other method or path under `/api/` returns `405` or `404` without reaching Strapi.
- Responses under `/api/` carry `Cache-Control: no-store`; no `proxy_cache` is configured.
  `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`; hashed build assets may be cached long-term
  (their names change on every build).
- Requests carrying an `Authorization` header are rejected (`400`), so the proxy can never be used
  to replay a token from a browser.

**Strapi rules (bootstrap code, idempotent, applied on every start; no manual admin clicks)**

- Public role: **exactly** `api::country.country.find` and `api::form-field.form-field.find` in
  US-01 (US-02 adds `api::plan.plan.find`, US-03 `api::terms.terms.find`). No `findOne`: the app
  never reads a single document by `documentId`. Justification per permission is in the table
  below. Bootstrap reconciles the role to this list (removes anything else) on every start.
- The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.callback`, `auth.connect`,
  `auth.forgotPassword`, `auth.resetPassword`, `auth.register`, `auth.emailConfirmation`,
  `auth.sendEmailConfirmation`, `auth.refresh`) are removed, and the advanced setting
  `allow_register` is set to `false`. Verified in `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`:
  `services/users-permissions.js` (`DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`) and `bootstrap/index.js`
  (`allow_register: true` by default). The app has no end-user accounts, so these endpoints are
  unneeded attack surface. Note: the plugin recreates its defaults only when the permissions table
  is empty (`syncPermissions`), which never happens while our `find` permissions exist.
- The authenticated role gets no content permissions.
- **Published only for anonymous reads.** The REST API accepts `status=draft` from any caller
  that has `find` (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `content-api-constants.js` lists `status` as an
  allowed query parameter; `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `core-api/service/core-service.js` defaults it to
  `published` only when absent; the Strapi REST docs page on `status` states no permission
  requirement for `status=draft`). With a plain public `find`, anyone could read drafts with
  `?status=draft`. A Strapi global middleware therefore removes `status`, `publicationFilter` and
  `hasPublishedVersion` from content API requests that are not authenticated by an API token, so
  the default (`published`) always applies to anonymous reads.
- CORS (`strapi::cors`, default `origin: '*'` in `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `middlewares/cors.js`) is
  restricted to an environment-driven allow-list, empty by default: the browser reaches the
  content API same-origin through nginx and never needs CORS.
- Strapi creates a default "Full Access" API token on a fresh database with no admin user and no
  token (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `bootstrap.js`, `createDefaultAPITokensIfNeeded`). It never
  reaches the browser, but it is an unused write credential: bootstrap deletes the default
  "Full Access" token, and it is never copied into any `.env`.

| Public permission | Why it is needed | Data exposed |
|---|---|---|
| `api::country.country.find` | Chooser, unknown-country links, currency and locale (ADR-0001); required by Strapi to filter `form-field` by `country.code` | Country code, name, currency, locale. Public by nature. |
| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | Step 1 form (US-01-BR-01) | Labels, rules, options, Spanish copy. Public by nature (shown to every visitor). |

**Caching**

- No HTTP cache interceptor and no service worker caching of `/api/` in Angular; content is loaded
  once per full page load and held in memory (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001).
- No Strapi REST cache plugin. Strapi 5.63.0 core sets no `Cache-Control` on content API
  responses (no occurrence in `@strapi/core@5.63.0/dist`); nginx adds `no-store`.

**End-to-end writes for AC-03 (US-01-Q-23)**

- The write credential exists only in the **Playwright Node process**. Flow:
  1. Bootstrap creates a development super admin from `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL` /
     `STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` when no admin user exists (fictitious values in `.env.example`; real
     `.env` git-ignored). The human uses the same account at HC3.
  2. The test's setup logs in to the admin API (`POST /admin/login`, verified in
     `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `routes/authentication.js`; the response includes an access token)
     directly against Strapi's port, not through nginx.
  3. It creates a **custom** API token (`POST /admin/api-tokens`, type `custom`, verified in
     `routes/api-tokens.js` and `services/constants.js`: types `read-only`, `full-access`,
     `custom`) scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`, with the shortest
     lifespan Strapi accepts (7 days; the validator accepts only `null`, 7, 30 or 90 days).
  4. It creates the `mobilePhone` field with `POST /api/form-fields` on Strapi's port. A REST
     `POST` publishes immediately unless `status=draft` is passed (Strapi REST docs, `status`
     page), which is what AC-03 needs.
  5. Teardown deletes the field and then the token (`DELETE /admin/api-tokens/:id`), also when the
     test fails.
- The token and the admin JWT are never passed to `page.evaluate`, `page.route`,
  `addInitScript`, cookies or storage of the browser context. The browser under test talks only to
  nginx, which rejects any `Authorization` header and any non-GET method.

### Consequences

- Good, because no token of any kind is ever sent by the browser or stored on disk by the app (D1).
- Good, because the same build runs in compose, in `ng serve` and in any future host: the API path
  is relative (D2).
- Good, because drafts stay unreadable even when someone calls Strapi's port directly with
  `?status=draft` (D5).
- Good, because one start command is enough: no token has to be generated and copied before the
  front end works (D4).
- Bad, because anyone who can reach Strapi's port can call the two public `find` endpoints
  directly, bypassing the proxy's allow-list — mitigation: the data is public by nature, drafts are
  blocked in Strapi, and the role has no other permission. Rate limiting is out of scope.
- Bad, because the published-only rule is custom middleware that a Strapi upgrade could make
  incomplete (for example a new publication query parameter) — mitigation: an automated check
  (below) requests the seeded draft field anonymously; re-verify on every Strapi upgrade.
- Bad, because the e2e setup depends on Strapi's admin API (`/admin/login`, `/admin/api-tokens`),
  which is what the admin panel uses but is less documented than the REST API — mitigation: it is
  used only by tests; if it changes, only the AC-03 test breaks, and the HC3 manual check of AC-03
  in the admin remains.
- Bad, because a development admin account is created from environment variables — mitigation:
  fictitious values only in `.env.example`, `.env` git-ignored, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh`.
- Neutral: nginx is needed anyway to serve the Angular build; the proxy adds a few lines of
  configuration, not a new service.

### Strongest argument against

Strapi's own port, which stays open for the admin panel, still answers the public `find`
endpoints to anyone who can reach it, and those requests skip the proxy's method and path
allow-list entirely. On that port, keeping drafts hidden rests only on custom published-only
middleware, which a Strapi upgrade could quietly make incomplete (for example through a new
publication query parameter) without any error. Option 3 (proxy-injected read-only token, empty
public role) would close Strapi's port to anonymous content reads altogether.

**Why we accept it:** the two exposed endpoints serve data that is public by nature, and the
public role has no other permission. Option 3 needs the token to exist before nginx starts,
which breaks the single start command (D4), and it gives the browser the same effective access
through the proxy, so its gain is limited to the direct port. The draft rule is guarded by an
automated anonymous request for the seeded draft field, re-run on every Strapi upgrade.

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27): every browser request to `/api/` is a `GET`, none has an
  `Authorization` header, none contains a step 1 value.
- Check in the same file (an API request from the Node process, no browser): anonymous
  `GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email` on Strapi's port returns no `email`
  field; `POST /api/form-fields` through nginx returns `405`.
- E2E `us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03) follows the write flow above; review checks that the
  token is created and deleted in Node only.
- Review checklist: bootstrap reconciles the public role to the table above; `allow_register` is
  `false`; no `Authorization` header and no Strapi host name in `frontend/src`;
  `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. Direct access with the public role

- Good, because there is no proxy configuration at all.
- Bad, because the browser needs Strapi's absolute address, so the build needs a runtime
  `config.json` fetched before bootstrap (`provideAppInitializer`, present in
  `@angular/core@22.3.0`), a second artefact per environment.
- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.

### 2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role (chosen)

- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.
- Good, because the API address is relative; CORS can be closed.
- Good, because method, path and cache rules sit in one reviewed file.
- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).

### 3. Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token

- Good, because the public role can be empty: Strapi's port answers `403` to anonymous content
  requests.
- Bad, because the token must exist before nginx starts: Strapi generates the key randomly at
  creation (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `services/api-token.js`, `crypto.randomBytes`), so a single
  `docker compose up` would need Strapi to write the secret to a shared volume or to insert a
  pre-hashed key using its internal hashing, both fragile (D4).
- Bad, because the `read-only` type grants `find`/`findOne` on **every** content type, including
  future ones, and `status=draft` is still accepted; a `custom` token narrows it, but the
  published-only rule is still needed.
- Bad, because the proxy then grants anyone who reaches it the token's rights, so the browser's
  effective access is the same as option 2: the security gain is only on Strapi's direct port.

## More Information

- Verified sources (2026-11-20; packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@strapi/admin@5.63.0`,
  `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`, `@angular/core@22.3.0` (files cited inline);
  https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/status (REST default `published`, `POST`/`PUT` publish
  unless `status=draft`); https://hub.docker.com/_/nginx (environment variables via templates).
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (which types are per country, and why `country` must be readable),
  ADR-0003 (step 1 values never leave the browser).
- Revisit when: the app gains end-user accounts, content that is not public appears, Strapi's
  port must be reachable from the internet without the proxy, or Strapi adds a permission for
  reading drafts through the content API.

# ADR-0005: Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002)

## Context and Problem Statement

ADR-0002 (Accepted) lets the AC-03 end-to-end test create a `form-field` through Strapi's own port
with a temporary `custom` API token scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`
only (ADR-0002, "End-to-end writes for AC-03", step 3). A `form-field` has a required `country`
relation (ADR-0001). In gate attempt 1 of US-01, `POST /api/form-fields` with
`country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` failed with `400 ValidationError "Invalid key country"`
(`details.key = "country"`, `source = "body"`). Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a relation key in the
input unless the caller may **read** the relation target. The strapi-developer confirmed at runtime
that the same payload succeeds once `api::country.country.find` is added to the token. This ADR
decides how the e2e write gets past that check. It amends ADR-0002 **only** in the scope of the
temporary e2e token. Everything else in ADR-0002 stays as it is. Story: US-01
(`specs/US-01/spec.md`, US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3; ADR-0002 D1). Any write credential stays minimal and lives only in the Playwright Node process.
- D2. AC-03 is automated: the test creates a published field linked to a country during the run, then deletes it (US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).
- D3. Keep bespoke code off security-relevant paths: every custom controller on a write endpoint has to be reviewed and re-verified on each Strapi upgrade (human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21; ADR-0002 already carries one such custom piece, the published-only middleware).
- D4. Do not change the public role or the read path decided in ADR-0002 (Accepted ADRs are binding, CLAUDE.md §1).

## Considered Options

1. **Widen the temporary token**: `form-field.create`, `form-field.delete` and
   `api::country.country.find` (read-only).
2. **Custom `form-field` create controller**: validate the payload without `country`, then attach
   one validated country `documentId` before calling the document service; the token keeps the
   ADR-0002 scope. Implemented in commit e5ba5ff, to be reverted.
3. **Admin API (content-manager) write path**: no content-API token at all; the test uses the admin
   JWT it already obtains in ADR-0002 step 2 and calls
   `POST /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/actions/publish` (create and
   publish in one request) and `DELETE /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/:id`.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find`"**, because it uses Strapi's
own relation-permission rule as designed and needs no custom code on a write endpoint (D3). The
only right it adds is a read of country data, which the public role already exposes (D1). The
AC-03 test then works with the stock controller (D2), and the public role and read path are
unchanged (D4).

### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0002, step 3 of "End-to-end writes for AC-03")

- The temporary `custom` API token created by the AC-03 test setup has exactly these permissions:
  `api::form-field.form-field.create`, `api::form-field.form-field.delete` and
  `api::country.country.find`. Nothing else. Lifespan and teardown stay as in ADR-0002 (7 days,
  deleted in teardown, also on failure).
- The custom `create` in `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` added by e5ba5ff
  is reverted to `factories.createCoreController('api::form-field.form-field')`.
- General rule for later stories: when a test token must write a document with relations, it gets
  `find` on each relation target, and on nothing more. ADR-0002's public role table does not
  change.

### Consequences

- Good, because the form-field write path is Strapi's stock controller again: input validation,
  sanitisation and the relation check all run unchanged (D3).
- Good, because the added permission matches what is already public. `api::country.country.find`
  is in the public role (ADR-0002 table), so the token learns nothing about published countries
  that an anonymous caller cannot learn.
- Bad, because the token's scope is no longer "write only". It now includes a read, and later
  stories will add one `find` per relation target (for example US-02 if a plan test writes plans
  with a `country` relation). Mitigation: the scope list sits in one place in the e2e setup, and
  review checks it against this ADR.
- Bad, because a token holder can read **draft** countries. The published-only middleware
  (`backend/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`) keeps publication parameters on any request that
  carries an `Authorization` header, so `GET /api/countries?status=draft` with this token returns
  drafts, which the public role cannot see. Mitigation: the token exists only in the Playwright
  Node process for the length of the test, is deleted in teardown, and country records hold no
  secret data (code, name, currency, locale).
- Neutral: Strapi checks the **token's own** permissions, not the public role's
  (`content-api-token.js` `verify`, see More Information). The public `country.find` therefore does
  not satisfy the check, and the token needs the permission itself.

### Strongest argument against

Option 3 removes the content-API write token altogether. ADR-0002 step 2 already logs in to the
admin API and holds an admin JWT in the Node process, and the content-manager can create, publish
and delete the field with that JWT. So there would be no token to scope, nothing to widen as
later stories add relations, no API token row to clean up, and the test would follow the same
path an editor takes in the admin panel, which is what AC-03 describes ("the business team adds
and publishes in Strapi a new field"). Option 1 keeps a second credential and adds to its scope.

**Why we accept it:** the admin JWT belongs to the bootstrap super admin, so it has every admin
permission. Making it the write credential swaps a narrow, expiring, deletable token for a
full-power session, which is worse under D1. The content-manager routes are also internal admin
APIs whose payload format (relation `connect` shapes, locale and status handling) is less
documented than the REST API, the same risk ADR-0002 accepted only for `/admin/login` and
`/admin/api-tokens`. Option 1 grants a read on data that is already public and keeps the test on
the content API that ADR-0002 chose. Option 3 stays the fallback if the token scope grows beyond a
few `find` permissions.

### Confirmation

- E2E `frontend/e2e/us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03): the token creation request lists exactly
  the three permissions above; the test creates the `mobilePhone` field with
  `country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` through the stock controller and gets `201`; teardown
  deletes the field and the token.
- Review checklist: `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` is the plain
  `createCoreController` (no custom `create`); the e2e token scope matches this ADR; the token and
  admin JWT never enter the browser context (ADR-0002 confirmation still applies).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find` (chosen)

- Good, because no custom code: Strapi's own `throwRestrictedRelations` check passes the normal
  way.
- Good, because the added right is read-only and matches the public role.
- Bad, because the scope grows with every relation target a test writes to.
- Bad, because the token can read draft countries (mitigated above).

### 2. Custom `form-field` create controller (commit e5ba5ff)

The controller pulls `country` out of `data`, runs `validateInput` and `sanitizeInput` on the
rest, then passes `country: <documentId>` straight to the document service.

- Good, because the token keeps the narrowest scope ADR-0002 wrote down (create and delete only).
- Good, because the document service still refuses an unknown `documentId`.
- Bad, because it deliberately bypasses Strapi's relation-permission check on a public write
  endpoint, for every caller that has `form-field.create`, not only the test. Any future token or
  role with that permission can then link a `form-field` to a country it cannot read.
- Bad, because it is bespoke security-relevant code (about 50 lines, its own relation-shape
  parser) to re-verify on every Strapi upgrade, against D3.
- Bad, because the same workaround would be needed again for every relation and every type a
  later test writes.

### 3. Admin API (content-manager) write path

Verified viable in `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0`: `dist/server/routes/admin.js` defines
`POST /collection-types/:model/actions/publish` (handler `collection-types.publish`, policies
`admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` and `explorer.publish`), and `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js`
`publish` creates the document when no `id` is given ("Create a new document and publish it in one
request"). `DELETE /collection-types/:model/:id` maps to `collection-types.delete`. These routes are
served under the `/content-manager` prefix on the admin API.

- Good, because no content-API write token exists at all, so there is nothing to scope or widen.
- Good, because it follows the same path an editor's click in the admin panel takes.
- Bad, because the credential is the super admin's JWT, with full admin rights, instead of a narrow
  expiring token (D1).
- Bad, because the content-manager API is internal to the admin panel and less documented, and its
  relation payload format was not exercised in this project.
- Bad, because it contradicts the write flow in ADR-0002 (steps 3 to 5) far more than a scope
  change does, so it would need a superseding ADR rather than an amendment.

## More Information

- Verified sources (2026-11-21; each package fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory
  outside the repo):
  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js`:
    `ACTIONS_TO_VERIFY = ['find']`; for a regular relation, `handleRegularRelation` builds the
    scope `` `${attribute.target}.find` `` and calls `strapi.auth.verify(auth, { scope })`; if it
    fails, `throwInvalidKey({ key, path })` raises the observed `Invalid key country`
    (`dist/validate/utils.js`, `throwInvalidKey`).
  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/index.js` `validateInput`: the restricted-relations
    visitor runs whenever the request has `auth` (`if (auth) { transforms.push(traverseEntity(throwRestrictedRelations(auth), …)) }`).
  - `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/core-api/controller/collection-type.js` `create` calls
    `this.validateInput(body.data, ctx)`, which delegates to `strapi.contentAPI.validate.input`
    (`dist/core-api/controller/index.js`).
  - `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `dist/server/server/src/strategies/content-api-token.js` `verify`: for a
    `custom` token, `scopes.every((scope) => ability.can(scope))`, so only the token's own
    permissions count (the public role is not consulted).
  - `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0` `dist/server/routes/admin.js` and
    `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js` (option 3, cited above).
- Runtime evidence (strapi-developer, gate attempt 1): the 400 body quoted in the context, and the
  `201` once `country.find` was added to the token.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (amended here, only step 3 of the AC-03 write flow; its index status
  becomes "Accepted (amended by ADR-0005)"), ADR-0001 (the `country` relation on per-country
  types).
- Revisit when: a test token needs `find` on a type that is not in the public role, the scope list
  grows beyond a handful of `find` permissions (then reconsider option 3 in a superseding ADR), or a
  Strapi upgrade changes `ACTIONS_TO_VERIFY` or the token `verify` logic.

# ADR-0002: Strapi access and security model

## Context and Problem Statement

The browser must read published content (countries and form fields in US-01, plans in US-02,
terms in US-03) from Strapi, and nothing else. We must decide how the browser reaches Strapi
(directly or through a proxy, anonymously or with a token), how the same build learns the API
address in every environment, how we avoid caches that would hide a newly published change, and
how the AC-03 end-to-end test creates content without a write credential ever reaching the
browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: US-01-AC-27, US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3). Evaluated as "token and permission security" (source: Assessment, evaluation).
- D2. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07). The build must not embed an environment-specific API address.
- D3. "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." (source: Assessment); visible on the next full page load, no cache delaying it (US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16).
- D4. "The whole project starts with a single command (for example docker compose up), with seed data for both countries" (source: Assessment, environment). Nothing may require a manual admin step to make the app work.
- D5. Drafts are never visible to end users (US-01-BR-06, US-01-AC-13).
- D6. AC-03 is automated: a test publishes a field during the run (US-01-Q-23), and the browser sees only GET requests without write tokens (US-01-AC-27).
- D7. Business editors use the Strapi admin, which must stay reachable (Assessment, business context).

## Considered Options

1. **Direct access with the public role**: the browser calls Strapi cross-origin with no token;
   the public role has `find`/`findOne` on the read types; the API URL comes from a runtime
   `config.json`.
2. **Same-origin nginx proxy + public role**: the nginx container that serves the Angular build
   forwards `GET /api/<allow-listed types>` to Strapi; the browser calls the relative path `/api`;
   Strapi's public role has only `find` on the read types and Strapi itself forces published
   content for anonymous requests.
3. **Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token**: the public role has no content
   permissions; nginx adds `Authorization: Bearer <read token>` to proxied requests; the token
   lives only in the proxy's environment.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role"**, because it meets D1 with no token
anywhere near the browser and no secret to provision at start-up (D4), gives the same build a
relative API address that works in every environment (D2), and places the cache and method rules
in one small config file (D3, D6). The extra safeguard that matters most, forcing published
content, is enforced **inside Strapi**, so it holds even for requests that bypass the proxy (D5,
D7).

### What is decided

**Topology (docker compose)**

- `frontend`: nginx (Docker Official Image) serving the Angular build on one origin, and proxying
  `/api/` to Strapi. The upstream address comes from an environment variable through the image's
  template mechanism (`/etc/nginx/templates/*.template` processed with `envsubst` into
  `/etc/nginx/conf.d` at container start; Docker Official Image "nginx" docs). The browser bundle
  contains no host name.
- `strapi`: exposes its own port for the admin panel used by editors (D7). The content API on that
  port is protected by the Strapi-side rules below, not by the proxy.
- Development (`ng serve`) uses the Angular dev-server proxy for `/api`, so the code path is the
  same relative URL. No `environment.ts` API URL, no runtime `config.json` (nothing to configure).

**Proxy rules (nginx)**

- Only `GET` (and the implicit `HEAD`) on an allow-list of paths: `/api/countries` and
  `/api/form-fields` in US-01; US-02 and US-03 add `/api/plans` and `/api/terms` through their
  specs. Any other method or path under `/api/` returns `405` or `404` without reaching Strapi.
- Responses under `/api/` carry `Cache-Control: no-store`; no `proxy_cache` is configured.
  `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`; hashed build assets may be cached long-term
  (their names change on every build).
- Requests carrying an `Authorization` header are rejected (`400`), so the proxy can never be used
  to replay a token from a browser.

**Strapi rules (bootstrap code, idempotent, applied on every start; no manual admin clicks)**

- Public role: **exactly** `api::country.country.find` and `api::form-field.form-field.find` in
  US-01 (US-02 adds `api::plan.plan.find`, US-03 `api::terms.terms.find`). No `findOne`: the app
  never reads a single document by `documentId`. Justification per permission is in the table
  below. Bootstrap reconciles the role to this list (removes anything else) on every start.
- The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.callback`, `auth.connect`,
  `auth.forgotPassword`, `auth.resetPassword`, `auth.register`, `auth.emailConfirmation`,
  `auth.sendEmailConfirmation`, `auth.refresh`) are removed, and the advanced setting
  `allow_register` is set to `false`. Verified in `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`:
  `services/users-permissions.js` (`DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`) and `bootstrap/index.js`
  (`allow_register: true` by default). The app has no end-user accounts, so these endpoints are
  unneeded attack surface. Note: the plugin recreates its defaults only when the permissions table
  is empty (`syncPermissions`), which never happens while our `find` permissions exist.
- The authenticated role gets no content permissions.
- **Published only for anonymous reads.** The REST API accepts `status=draft` from any caller
  that has `find` (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `content-api-constants.js` lists `status` as an
  allowed query parameter; `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `core-api/service/core-service.js` defaults it to
  `published` only when absent; the Strapi REST docs page on `status` states no permission
  requirement for `status=draft`). With a plain public `find`, anyone could read drafts with
  `?status=draft`. A Strapi global middleware therefore removes `status`, `publicationFilter` and
  `hasPublishedVersion` from content API requests that are not authenticated by an API token, so
  the default (`published`) always applies to anonymous reads.
- CORS (`strapi::cors`, default `origin: '*'` in `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `middlewares/cors.js`) is
  restricted to an environment-driven allow-list, empty by default: the browser reaches the
  content API same-origin through nginx and never needs CORS.
- Strapi creates a default "Full Access" API token on a fresh database with no admin user and no
  token (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `bootstrap.js`, `createDefaultAPITokensIfNeeded`). It never
  reaches the browser, but it is an unused write credential: bootstrap deletes the default
  "Full Access" token, and it is never copied into any `.env`.

| Public permission | Why it is needed | Data exposed |
|---|---|---|
| `api::country.country.find` | Chooser, unknown-country links, currency and locale (ADR-0001); required by Strapi to filter `form-field` by `country.code` | Country code, name, currency, locale. Public by nature. |
| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | Step 1 form (US-01-BR-01) | Labels, rules, options, Spanish copy. Public by nature (shown to every visitor). |

**Caching**

- No HTTP cache interceptor and no service worker caching of `/api/` in Angular; content is loaded
  once per full page load and held in memory (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001).
- No Strapi REST cache plugin. Strapi 5.63.0 core sets no `Cache-Control` on content API
  responses (no occurrence in `@strapi/core@5.63.0/dist`); nginx adds `no-store`.

**End-to-end writes for AC-03 (US-01-Q-23)**

- The write credential exists only in the **Playwright Node process**. Flow:
  1. Bootstrap creates a development super admin from `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL` /
     `STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` when no admin user exists (fictitious values in `.env.example`; real
     `.env` git-ignored). The human uses the same account at HC3.
  2. The test's setup logs in to the admin API (`POST /admin/login`, verified in
     `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `routes/authentication.js`; the response includes an access token)
     directly against Strapi's port, not through nginx.
  3. It creates a **custom** API token (`POST /admin/api-tokens`, type `custom`, verified in
     `routes/api-tokens.js` and `services/constants.js`: types `read-only`, `full-access`,
     `custom`) scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`, with the shortest
     lifespan Strapi accepts (7 days; the validator accepts only `null`, 7, 30 or 90 days).
  4. It creates the `mobilePhone` field with `POST /api/form-fields` on Strapi's port. A REST
     `POST` publishes immediately unless `status=draft` is passed (Strapi REST docs, `status`
     page), which is what AC-03 needs.
  5. Teardown deletes the field and then the token (`DELETE /admin/api-tokens/:id`), also when the
     test fails.
- The token and the admin JWT are never passed to `page.evaluate`, `page.route`,
  `addInitScript`, cookies or storage of the browser context. The browser under test talks only to
  nginx, which rejects any `Authorization` header and any non-GET method.

### Consequences

- Good, because no token of any kind is ever sent by the browser or stored on disk by the app (D1).
- Good, because the same build runs in compose, in `ng serve` and in any future host: the API path
  is relative (D2).
- Good, because drafts stay unreadable even when someone calls Strapi's port directly with
  `?status=draft` (D5).
- Good, because one start command is enough: no token has to be generated and copied before the
  front end works (D4).
- Bad, because anyone who can reach Strapi's port can call the two public `find` endpoints
  directly, bypassing the proxy's allow-list — mitigation: the data is public by nature, drafts are
  blocked in Strapi, and the role has no other permission. Rate limiting is out of scope.
- Bad, because the published-only rule is custom middleware that a Strapi upgrade could make
  incomplete (for example a new publication query parameter) — mitigation: an automated check
  (below) requests the seeded draft field anonymously; re-verify on every Strapi upgrade.
- Bad, because the e2e setup depends on Strapi's admin API (`/admin/login`, `/admin/api-tokens`),
  which is what the admin panel uses but is less documented than the REST API — mitigation: it is
  used only by tests; if it changes, only the AC-03 test breaks, and the HC3 manual check of AC-03
  in the admin remains.
- Bad, because a development admin account is created from environment variables — mitigation:
  fictitious values only in `.env.example`, `.env` git-ignored, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh`.
- Neutral: nginx is needed anyway to serve the Angular build; the proxy adds a few lines of
  configuration, not a new service.

### Strongest argument against

Strapi's own port, which stays open for the admin panel, still answers the public `find`
endpoints to anyone who can reach it, and those requests skip the proxy's method and path
allow-list entirely. On that port, keeping drafts hidden rests only on custom published-only
middleware, which a Strapi upgrade could quietly make incomplete (for example through a new
publication query parameter) without any error. Option 3 (proxy-injected read-only token, empty
public role) would close Strapi's port to anonymous content reads altogether.

**Why we accept it:** the two exposed endpoints serve data that is public by nature, and the
public role has no other permission. Option 3 needs the token to exist before nginx starts,
which breaks the single start command (D4), and it gives the browser the same effective access
through the proxy, so its gain is limited to the direct port. The draft rule is guarded by an
automated anonymous request for the seeded draft field, re-run on every Strapi upgrade.

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27): every browser request to `/api/` is a `GET`, none has an
  `Authorization` header, none contains a step 1 value.
- Check in the same file (an API request from the Node process, no browser): anonymous
  `GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email` on Strapi's port returns no `email`
  field; `POST /api/form-fields` through nginx returns `405`.
- E2E `us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03) follows the write flow above; review checks that the
  token is created and deleted in Node only.
- Review checklist: bootstrap reconciles the public role to the table above; `allow_register` is
  `false`; no `Authorization` header and no Strapi host name in `frontend/src`;
  `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. Direct access with the public role

- Good, because there is no proxy configuration at all.
- Bad, because the browser needs Strapi's absolute address, so the build needs a runtime
  `config.json` fetched before bootstrap (`provideAppInitializer`, present in
  `@angular/core@22.3.0`), a second artefact per environment.
- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.

### 2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role (chosen)

- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.
- Good, because the API address is relative; CORS can be closed.
- Good, because method, path and cache rules sit in one reviewed file.
- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).

### 3. Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token

- Good, because the public role can be empty: Strapi's port answers `403` to anonymous content
  requests.
- Bad, because the token must exist before nginx starts: Strapi generates the key randomly at
  creation (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `services/api-token.js`, `crypto.randomBytes`), so a single
  `docker compose up` would need Strapi to write the secret to a shared volume or to insert a
  pre-hashed key using its internal hashing, both fragile (D4).
- Bad, because the `read-only` type grants `find`/`findOne` on **every** content type, including
  future ones, and `status=draft` is still accepted; a `custom` token narrows it, but the
  published-only rule is still needed.
- Bad, because the proxy then grants anyone who reaches it the token's rights, so the browser's
  effective access is the same as option 2: the security gain is only on Strapi's direct port.

## More Information

- Verified sources (2026-11-20; packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@strapi/admin@5.63.0`,
  `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`, `@angular/core@22.3.0` (files cited inline);
  https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/status (REST default `published`, `POST`/`PUT` publish
  unless `status=draft`); https://hub.docker.com/_/nginx (environment variables via templates).
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (which types are per country, and why `country` must be readable),
  ADR-0003 (step 1 values never leave the browser).
- Revisit when: the app gains end-user accounts, content that is not public appears, Strapi's
  port must be reachable from the internet without the proxy, or Strapi adds a permission for
  reading drafts through the content API.
